This app provides real-time GPS coordinates to your camera via Bluetooth, allowing for automatic geotagging of your photos without needing a camera's built-in GPS.
Check the app logs in the top menu for troubleshooting information, or review your device settings to ensure all permissions are granted.
How do I connect my camera to the app?

1. Make sure your camera supports Bluetooth connectivity and GPS tagging
2. Enable Bluetooth on your camera and phone
3. Put your camera in pairing mode, click on the camera on the main screen and follow the on-screen instructions (both camera and phone) 
 4. If this fails, remove any pairing in the Bluetooth settings of the phone and camera. Then try again
Why isn't my camera appearing in the list?

• Ensure your camera is in pairing/Bluetooth mode
• Check that your camera supports the required Bluetooth profile
• Make sure you're within range (typically 10 meters)
• Try restarting Bluetooth on your phone
My camera is losing connection all the time

Try these solutions:
• Keep your phone closer to the camera
• Disable battery optimization for the app
• Check whether your camera has power-saving modes that affect Bluetooth
• Restart both devices and pair them again if needed
How do I enable the service permanently? It seems to stop after a while

Please visit the App Settings and try the options in the Battery & Background section. Alternatively try the following: 
To keep GPS data syncing with your camera:
1. Go to your device's Settings > Apps
2. Find 'AlphaGPS' in the app list
3. Tap on it and select 'Battery'
4. Choose 'Don't optimize' or 'Allow background activity'
5. This prevents the system from stopping the GPS service

You can also access this through the device details page in the app.
My camera does not connect automatically, what can I do?

Unfortunately, there might be situations, where the automatic connection does not work. If you encounter issues please do the following: On the main screen, tap on your camera to open the details screen. There you have an option to enable the "Always On" mode, which will keep the app in the foreground. \nOtherwise try toggling bluetooth or remove the device from the app and associate it again.
What permissions does the app need?

The app requires:
• Location permissions (for GPS data)
• Bluetooth permissions (to connect to camera)
• Nearby devices permission (for device discovery and the camera's Wi-Fi)
• Notification permission (for the status notification)
• Battery optimization exemption (optional, for continuous service)
How accurate is the GPS data?

GPS accuracy depends on:
• Satellite visibility (better outdoors)
• Weather conditions
• Your phone's GPS capabilities
• Typical accuracy is 3–5 meters under good conditions
Does the app work in the background?

Yes, once properly configured:
• The service runs in the background to maintain GPS sync
• Make sure to disable battery optimization
• Pressing Home, switching apps or swiping the app away does not disconnect the camera
• The app will show a persistent notification when active
• GPS data is continuously sent to your connected camera
Tap here for Step-by-step fixes for the most common issues.
Enable location & time zone linking (older cameras)
On cameras with the older menu layout (e.g. α6400, ZV-E10, α6100, α7 III) location linking must be switched on manually. Newer cameras activate it automatically when the app connects.
On the camera, turn on location linking:
MENU → Network → Loc. Info. Link Set. → Location Info. Link → On
To also take over time and time zone from the phone, enable both options in the same menu:
Auto Time Correct. → On • Auto Area Adjust. → On
If the menu items are grayed out or linking still fails, turn off the Bluetooth remote — see section 3.
Sony Help Guide: Loc. Info. Link Set. (α6400)
Sony Help Guide: Location Info. Link Set. (ZV-E10)
Camera connects but GPS doesn't work

Typical when the camera was set up with Sony's Creators' App or Imaging Edge Mobile before: the phone is already paired with the camera, so no new pairing is requested — but location transfer doesn't work properly with AlphaGPS. Removing the old pairing everywhere fixes this.
Remove the camera from your phone's Bluetooth settings:
Settings → Connected devices (Bluetooth) → your camera → Forget
On the camera, delete the old pairing (older models don't have this menu item — there, pairing again simply replaces the old connection):
MENU → Network → Bluetooth → Manage Paired Device
If a Sony app is still installed, remove the camera there as well:
Set up the camera again in AlphaGPS: put it into pairing mode and start a new scan.
Turn off the Bluetooth remote (older cameras)

Cameras like the α6400 cannot use the Bluetooth remote and location linking at the same time — with the remote on, the connection or GPS transfer stops working. Newer models (e.g. α7 IV and later) support both.
On the camera, switch the Bluetooth remote off:
MENU → Network → Bluetooth Rmt Ctrl → Off
AlphaGPS no longer uses the remote control feature — only the camera setting above matters.
Sony Help Guide: Bluetooth Rmt Ctrl (α6400)
If photos are tagged with a position that is noticeably off, the app usually isn't allowed to use your precise location.
Settings → Apps → AlphaGPS → Permissions → Location → Use precise location
Exclude the app from battery optimization so transmission keeps running in the background: Settings → Apps → AlphaGPS → Battery → Unrestricted.
Camera starts slowly or its screen stays black
On some cameras, allowing smartphone connections while the camera is off can delay startup when AlphaGPS is enabled.

In the camera's Network menu, set 'Cnct. while Power OFF' or 'Cnct. during Power OFF' to Off. The name and menu location vary by model. This disables smartphone access while the camera is off; keep Bluetooth enabled for GPS and time sync when the camera is on.
This often happens when the camera is not in pairing mode or is still paired with another device:
• Put the camera into pairing mode: MENU → Network → Bluetooth → Pairing.
• On the camera, delete old pairings: MENU → Network → Bluetooth → Manage Paired Device.
• Remove the camera from your phone's Bluetooth settings (Settings → Bluetooth), then try again.

Camera not found? Make sure it is in pairing mode. If it was set up with Sony's Creators' App or Imaging Edge Mobile before, remove the old pairing from the camera and from your phone's Bluetooth settings — the troubleshooting guide walks you through it.

The app itself does not collect or upload any data, and it has no crash reporting or analytics. Position and time come from the system location service (GPS, and network or fused positioning where the system provides it — how those work is determined by the system and the device vendor's settings, not by this app). The app keeps no separate location history or tracks of its own; position and time are only sent over Bluetooth to the camera you have paired, and collection stops as soon as the camera disconnects. Browsing and downloading photos uses the camera's own Wi-Fi, point to point, without going through the internet. Photos you take with the camera may contain location data the camera wrote into them. Photos you download are saved only on this device. The external links on the About page (the GitHub project and the upstream author's sponsor page) open in your browser and are covered by those sites' own privacy policies. Nothing is sent to the developer or any third party.
